text.en: Melita, a Minos pack-herder, has entered a cooperative agreement with Rhodes Island alongside her packbeast. Melita herself is responsible for providing guidance and assistance with Rhodes Island's livestock farming operations, while the packbeast additionally provides transport and haulage services.
text.zh: 梅里塔，米诺斯牧驮人，携驮兽与罗德岛达成合作。梅里塔本人负责为罗德岛的经济动物养殖业务提供指导与帮助，驮兽则额外提供驮行运输等服务。

text.en:
Imaging tests show blurred organ outlines and abnormal shadows in the operator's thoracic cavity, with abnormal particulate counts in the circulatory system, indicating signs of Oripathy infection. The subject is confirmed at this stage as an Infected.

[Cell-Originium Fusion Rate] 4%
Operator Tin Man has no bodily crystals in the conventional sense, but some of the hair on her body shows a tendency toward crystallization.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.20 u/L
Acute infection in early childhood caused the lesions to spread to multiple vital organs throughout her body. Although her condition has stabilized, excessive stimulation is likely to cause fatal deterioration in a short period.
"What else did you expect from a kid who grew up scratching and clawing her way through the battlefield?"

Note: Clinical diagnosis analysis of the packbeast can be found in the archive attachment.
"What else did you expect from a retired military packbeast?"
text.zh:
造影检测结果显示，该干员体内脏器轮廓模糊，可见异常阴影，循环系统内源石颗粒检测异常，有矿石病感染迹象，现阶段可确认为矿石病感染者。

【体细胞与源石融合率】4%
干员行铃没有常规意义上的体表结晶，但其体表部分毛发表现出结晶化倾向。

【血液源石结晶密度】0.20u/L
幼年时的急性感染经历使病灶扩散到了体内多处重要器官。虽然病情已趋向稳定，但过度刺激很可能在短时间内导致致命的恶化。
“战场上摸爬滚打长大的孩子，你指望是什么结果呢。”

另：驮兽的临床诊断分析见档案附件。
“退役下来的军用驮兽，你又指望是什么结果呢。”

text.en:
Rest assured, Melita is doing just fine.
Did you see the photo attached to the letter?
No need to doubt it, that's Melita.
Head-to-toe in a full suit, even wearing the kind of fake horns Lady Lidia only puts on for formal occasions—that's Melita, leading a packbeast to host an exhibition at the International Livestock Expo.
Draped in robes hand-embroidered by the priest, holding a golden spear high, blowing a horn with a blast that shakes the heavens—that's Melita too, leading a packbeast to serve as the honor guard for a temple inauguration ceremony.
Squeezed into city guard armor, an electric baton in one hand and a riot shield in the other, soberly reporting coordinates over the walkie-talkie—that's still Melita, executing an armed cash-transport mission from Corinthia to Aseynus with her packbeast.
Oh, and there's also a picture of her arm-wrestling with Sinisca. Would you believe it, she actually won—though she was diagnosed with a hairline fracture the very same day. Fortunately, Sinisca kept her promise and temporarily replaced the mascot of the Lacedaemon Games with Melita's packbeasts.
Now everyone knows her. Every time they hear the clatter of packbeast hooves, people can't help pushing open their windows to see what kind of commotion this kid has stirred up this time.
The kid's got a million tricks. If you ask me, wandering the wastes for half her life hasn't stopped her from making a booming success of herself in the city.
Writing all this to you, I got to thinking—is there anything this kid can't figure out how to tinker with?
Well, thinking about it, there is. When it comes to packbeasts, she's still just as helpless. She did put in a ton of effort to finally learn how to communicate with one of the packbeasts, but even that one still doesn't listen to her much. The others... well, don't even ask. I honestly have no idea how she keeps doing this line of work.
—A letter addressed to the rancher who leased a pasture at a discount to Melita back in the day
text.zh:
放一万个心，梅里塔好着呢。
随信寄过去的照片你看了吗？
不用怀疑，那都是梅里塔。
从头到脚一整套西装，甚至戴着里底娅小姐在正式场合才会戴的那种假角——那是梅里塔，带着驮兽在主持国际畜牧业展会的展演呢。
身上披着祭司亲手绣的长袍，手里拄着黄金长矛，嘴上的号角吹得震天响——那也是梅里塔，带着驮兽在充当神殿落成仪式的仪仗队呢。
套在城邦卫兵的盔甲里面，一手电棍一手防爆盾，朝对讲机一本正经地汇报坐标——那还是梅里塔，带着驮兽在执行从科林尼亚到雅赛努斯的武装运钞任务呢。
哦，还有一张她和西妮斯卡掰手腕的。你敢信吗，她甚至掰赢了——虽然当天就确诊了骨裂。好在西妮斯卡信守承诺，临时把拉刻代蒙运动会的吉祥物换成了她的驮兽们。
现在大家都认识她了。每次听到驮兽蹄声，大家都忍不住要推开窗户，看看这孩子又折腾出了什么名堂。
孩子办法多着呢。要我看，她在野地里流浪了半辈子，一点儿也不影响她在城里混得风生水起。
给你写这些的时候，我脑子里在想，还有什么是这孩子捣鼓不明白的吗？
想了想还是有的。对驮兽，她还是那么没招。她倒是费老大力气终于学会了跟其中一只驮兽交流，但就那一只，也还是不怎么听她的。其他的……就更别说了。真不知道这孩子是怎么一直干得下去这行儿的。
——一封信，寄给当年那位把牧场打折承包给梅里塔的牧场主

text.en:
Packbeasts.
These magnificent creatures have walked the earth for tens of millions of years, their hooves shaping the landscape long before Catastrophes ever did.
At what point did humanity become that special footnote in their evolutionary journey?
That story begins with the very first person who climbed onto a packbeast's back.
"When faced with Catastrophes, human foot speed is vastly inferior to animals. To escape in time, people found a way to 'hitch a ride,' mounting the animals later known as 'packbeasts,'" noted scholar Mr. Erickson tells us.
So why didn't the packbeasts shake our ancestors off? Mr. Erickson believes: "Their excessively heavy frames destined them from the start to be incapable of nimbly shaking off the uninvited guests clinging to them."
Yet perhaps another truth lies hidden within this ancient tale.
During our shoot in Minos, we met a rancher. A young girl named Melita, she grew up scavenging on the front lines of the war between Minos and Sargon. It was during this period that she befriended those military packbeasts who were likewise wandering the battlefield. She shared her scavenged food with the packbeasts, and in return, the packbeasts protected her like cubs, driving away ill-intentioned scavengers and fanged beasts. Melita and her packbeasts were companions surviving together through peril.
Did the earliest humans fleeing Catastrophes also provide packbeasts with some form of convenience, some assistance, some catalyst for survival? Were humans and packbeasts companions in survival from the very beginning? The lakes and marshes of eastern Sargon might hold the answer to that question...
—The phenomenal nature documentary "Living with the Earth"

"Hmph... It would've been better if those packbeasts had shaken people off back then. If they'd done that, they wouldn't be getting shipped off to the battlefield en masse nowadays."
"And what about you?"
"Then I would've been a happy kid who could keep everything she found all to herself. I probably would've grown a lot taller than I am now, too."
"But in that case, you wouldn't have this ranch or these packbeasts now.
"Yeah. But there definitely would've been some other easier job out there."
"Still, the person interviewed in the documentary was you, right?"
"It was. It's just that there are unusually many newborns on the ranch this year, and packbeast feed happened to go up in price... The production crew was introduced by that guy Periander, and they were paying way too much to turn down."
—Tin Man snatched the remote control to change the channel, speaking thusly to Pallas beside her
text.zh:
驮兽。
这种伟大的生灵已经行走大地千万年之久，它们的蹄比天灾更早地塑造了土地的形貌。
人类，是什么时候成为它们演化途中那个特殊的脚注的呢？
故事要从第一个爬上驮兽脊背的人讲起。
“面对天灾，人类的脚力远远比不上动物，为了能及时逃离，人们找到了‘搭顺风车’的方法，他们骑上的就是后来被称作‘驮兽’的动物。”知名学者埃里克森先生这样告诉我们。
那么，为什么驮兽没有把我们的祖先甩下来呢？埃里克森先生认为：“过于沉重的身躯注定了它们不能灵活地甩脱攀附其上的不速之客。”
但或许，这个古老的故事还存在另一种真相。
在米诺斯拍摄期间，我们结识了一位牧场主。这位名叫梅里塔的少女，从小在米诺斯与萨尔贡的交战前线上拾荒长大。也是在这期间，她结识了那些同样在战场上流浪的军用驮兽。她把采集来的食物分给驮兽们，驮兽们则像保护幼崽那样，为她驱逐不怀好意的拾荒者和牙兽。梅里塔与她的驮兽们，是在险境中共同求生的伙伴。
最初躲避天灾的人类，是否也为驮兽提供了某种便利、某种帮助、某种生存的契机？人类与驮兽，是否从最开始就是共同求生的伙伴？萨尔贡东部的湖沼里，或许藏着问题的答案……
——现象级自然纪录片《与大地共生》

“哼……那驮兽当初还是把人甩下来的好。当初要是那么干了，现在也就不会被大批大批地送上战场了。”
“那你呢？”
“那我当年就会是一个找到什么都能独享的快乐小孩。搞不好能比现在长得高很多哦？”
“但那样的话，你现在就没有这座牧场和这些驮兽了。”
“是啊。但肯定会有别的更轻松的活儿可做啊。”
“但纪录片里接受采访的那个人确实是你吧？”
“是我。这不是今年牧场里新生的崽子格外多，驮兽饲料又恰好涨价嘛……摄制组是佩里安德洛斯那家伙介绍来的，他们给的实在太多了。”
——行铃抢过遥控器换台之后，与身边的帕拉斯如是说道

text.en:
Tin Man has a pile of unpacked suitcases and an unfinished booklet. Naturally, a child who grew up struggling in the cracks between worlds always has these things, hoping that one day they can use them to fly far away to a better place.
Except Tin Man's things aren't meant for that.
This story starts with Broccoli. Regardless of how much effort was expended beforehand, the fact that Tin Man was eventually able to engage in a smooth conversation with Broccoli was nothing short of a miracle. Only, after that, not a single other packbeast could communicate smoothly with her.
Broccoli refused to pass messages from Tin Man to other packbeasts, telling her to "figure it out yourself." So Tin Man began trying to talk to other packbeasts, and that trial lasted for nearly a year.
Another packbeast named Carrot had an even more eccentric temper than Broccoli. No matter the reason or where they were headed, the moment she pulled the reins, he would stubbornly stiffen his neck and pick a fight; but if she coaxed him gently, he would vanish without a trace in the blink of an eye. To this day, whenever midnight escapades to hunt down packbeasts come up, Tin Man still can't help grinding her back teeth in vexation.
Everyone around Tin Man had grown used to this "antagonism." If there was ever a time she wasn't stomping around shouting Carrot's name while searching for her packbeast, they would find it strange.
Then, without any warning, on a completely ordinary afternoon, people saw Carrot calmly walking behind Tin Man, as docile as if he weren't even himself.

That kid suddenly came running to me to interpret a dream... It really was unusual. She never used to believe in these things, and even during the New Year when everyone gathered at the temple for dream interpretations, she'd always skip it.
She said she dreamed of Carrot traveling all by himself through countless places she didn't recognize—deserts, snow-capped mountains, forests, and iron cities bristling with furnaces.
In those dreams, she kept hearing the crisp sound of a bell ringing endlessly in the distance, as if calling out to Carrot.
Even I couldn't tell whether those dreams were true oracles. They weren't as hazy as ordinary dreams, yet far less clear than past oracles. I had nothing to tell the child, so I simply handed her an instructional ritual handbell from the temple. Fortunately, the moment she got the bell she was utterly overjoyed, without asking any extra questions.
—Cassandra, priestess of Aseynus

At the moment she shook the handbell, Tin Man was dumbfounded. Carrot obediently ambled over, looking as docile as if he weren't even himself.
And just like that, Tin Man inexplicably managed to communicate with a second packbeast. No one knew how she would manage to communicate with the next packbeast, or how much longer it would take.
Yet Tin Man herself didn't seem to be in a rush. She excitedly told you that once she filled those suitcases with essential daily supplies and filled her booklet with makeshift memo notes for asking directions, she would let Carrot go out and travel.
"What do you think, Carrot?" You shook the handbell in your hand and asked.
Carrot let out a bewildered snort, lowered his head, and nudged against your trouser leg, appearing quite pleased.
text.zh:
行铃有一堆没整理完的行李箱，和一本没写完的小册子。当然，像她这样在夹缝里挣扎着长大的孩子，总是会有这些东西，他们都盼着某一天凭这些东西远走高飞，去个更好的地方。
只不过，行铃的这些东西，不是用来干这个的。
事情又要从花椰菜说起。不论事先费了多大力气，行铃最终能顺畅地和花椰菜展开对话，确实堪称奇迹。只是在此之后，就再也没有第二只驮兽能跟她顺畅地交流了。
花椰菜拒绝替行铃给其他驮兽传话，让她“自己，办法”。行铃于是开始了和其他驮兽对话的尝试，这一试，就是将近一年。
那只名叫胡萝卜的驮兽脾气之古怪更甚花椰菜，不论是为了什么、要带他去哪，要是扯一下缰绳，他就立刻梗起脖子跟人较劲；但要是好言相劝，眨眼的工夫他就逃得无影无踪。时至今日，提起那些三更半夜出门找驮兽的经历，行铃还是会忍不住把后槽牙磨得嚓嚓作响。
这种“对抗”，行铃身边的人都已经习以为常。如果哪次没见她气冲冲地喊着胡萝卜的名字找驮兽，才会觉得奇怪。
然后，毫无征兆地，就在某个再平常不过的下午，人们看见胡萝卜平静地跟在行铃身后，温顺得简直不像他自己。

那孩子突然跑来找我解梦……确实反常。她平常都不信这些的，就连新年大家集体来神殿解梦的场合，她也总是缺席。
她说她梦见胡萝卜自己一只驮兽在很多她不认识的地方旅行，沙漠啊、雪山啊、森林啊，还有满是火炉的钢铁城市。
在那些梦里，她总能听到有清脆的铃声，像是在呼唤胡萝卜似的，在远方响个不停。
连我也说不上那些梦是不是真的神谕。它们不像寻常梦境那样模糊，又远不如以往的神谕那般清晰。我没什么能告诉那孩子的，只好从神殿里拿了一只仪式用的摇铃给她。好在，她拿到摇铃就开心得不得了，也没多问什么。
——雅赛努斯的祭司卡珊卓拉

晃动摇铃的那一刻，行铃傻了眼。胡萝卜听话地走了过来，温顺得简直不像他自己。
就这样，行铃莫名其妙地跟第二只驮兽交流上了。谁也不知道，她再跟下一只驮兽交流会是以什么样的方式，又还需要多久。
不过，行铃自己似乎并不着急。她兴冲冲地告诉你，等她把那些行李箱都填满了必要的生活用品，册子上也都写好了问路用的便签，她就放胡萝卜出去旅行。
“胡萝卜，你觉得呢？”你晃了晃手里的摇铃，问道。
胡萝卜懵懂地哼了两声，低下头在你的裤脚处蹭了蹭，似乎很是高兴。

text.en:
Good grief, look at those teeth of hers.
When Priestess Cassandra "escorted" her to our clinic, I was actually prepared. A wild kid who grew up wandering the battlefield, how good could her teeth possibly be?
But when we actually pried her mouth open and looked inside... you instantly understood why jagged teeth are called jagged.
I tried to explain to her that filing down sharp teeth is a perfectly normal lifestyle habit for us, essentially meant to adapt to modern dietary structures. I understood that while wandering, she needed a mouthful of sharp teeth to intimidate others, protect herself, and tear into whatever... food she could find. But now, after all, she lived in Aseynus... She repeated "I understand" over and over, and then wouldn't let me touch her.
That shouldn't be right, though? Didn't Priestess Cassandra say she was very sensible and had already adapted well to city life?
—A dentist at a dental clinic in Aseynus

Toothpicks cheap
Toothpicks combo pack
Dental floss picks good quality
Dental floss picks snap-resistant
Dental picks metal
...—Tin Man's shopping app search history

Not all newborn packbeasts born on the ranch are healthy.
Those poor wretches born sick or disabled simply can't be raised. Everyone in the trade told me such babies should just be put down early so they don't have to suffer.
...I wish there were miracles in this wasteland too! Packbeast babies that others are forced to put down, I could save them, nurse them back to health.
But the heroes of Minos probably aren't in the business of granting wishes like that. Reality is reality.
The first time I tried to put down a packbeast baby, I didn't manage it on the first try. It choked on blood, whimpered intermittently, and crawled toward my feet. Maybe I didn't have enough strength, or wasn't tall enough. After that, I never used that method again.
I could snap its neck with a single bite; that was something I'd been good at since I was little. If it didn't even let out a whimper, then it probably didn't suffer too much. Probably.
That's why I need these teeth. Don't ask again.
—Tin Man
text.zh:
天哪，她那口牙啊。
卡珊卓拉祭司把她“扭送”到我们诊所的时候，我其实有心理准备的。战场上流浪长大的野孩子嘛，牙能好到哪儿去呢。
但，真把她的嘴掰开，往里看一眼……你一下就明白锯齿为什么叫锯齿了。
我试着跟她解释，修整尖牙是我们再正常不过的生活习惯，本质上是为了适应当代的饮食结构。我理解她流浪的时候需要这一嘴的尖牙才能恐吓别人、保护自己，以及撕咬她能找到的那些……食物。但现在，她毕竟已经住在雅赛努斯了……她一口一个明白了，然后不让我碰。
不应该啊？卡珊卓拉祭司不是说她特别懂事、已经很适应城市生活了吗？
——雅赛努斯某牙科诊所的医生

牙签 便宜
牙签 组合装
牙线棒 好用
牙线棒 不容易断
剔牙针 金属
……
——行铃的采购平台搜索记录

牧场里出生的小驮兽崽子，并不都是健健康康的。
那些生出来就染病、残疾的倒霉蛋，是养不活的。同行都告诉我，这种崽子只能早点摔死，叫他们少受点苦。
……我也想大地上有那种奇迹啊！别人不得不摔死的驮兽崽子，我能救活了，养好了。
但米诺斯的英雄们大概都不负责实现这种愿望吧。现实就是现实。
我第一次试着摔驮兽崽子的时候，一下没摔死。他呛了血，断断续续地叫唤着，往我脚底下爬。可能是我力气不够大，或者长得不够高吧。那之后我就再不用摔的了。
我能一口咬断他的脖子，那是我从小就擅长的东西。如果他哼都没哼出一声来，那应该没有很受苦吧。大概。
所以我需要这口牙，别再问了。
——行铃

text.en:
Both times you told her the news of her promotion, she laughed it off and brushed it aside with silly banter. But when it actually came to the promotion ceremony, as she took the badge from your hands, she wiped it clean with her sleeve and started fiddling with it in her hands, as if she didn't quite know where it should be hung.
Is something wrong? You asked her.
She looked at you, looked at the badge, and couldn't quite articulate an answer.
A moment later, she bounced right back to her usual lively self, so you didn't give it much more thought. When she brought up that badge again later on, you were even momentarily stunned.
She knew what was wrong now, she said.
If things had gone differently, if Broccoli and those other packbeasts hadn't been abandoned on the battlefield and never met her, they probably would have been rounded up for auction after the war. The ones still healthy enough would be bought by people for farm work, and the rest slaughtered on the spot to be sold cheap as meat. Afterward, the beast-master in charge of the packbeasts in the military would receive a medal of merit personally issued by a priest, symbolizing the endorsement of a hero.
In her eyes, that's always what a badge was. Yet from then until now, the only thing she and the packbeasts had ever done was scratch and claw to stay alive. And staying alive probably wasn't the sort of thing that warranted a medal and reward.
So what should be done with the badge? You asked.
It's already been handed over to Lady Lidia, she said. The last time the government conducted a citizen census, since she had neither a birth certificate nor identification documents, she just handed that badge over.
"Somebody gave me this thing to reward me for trying extra hard to stay alive. So you lot can just use it as that proof—proof that I was born, that I'm alive, and that I haven't died—whatever you folks need it to be."
text.zh:
你两次告诉她晋升消息的时候，她都嘻嘻哈哈，说些有的没的就过去了。但真到了晋升仪式上，从你手里接过徽章时，她用袖套擦了擦，又拿回手里摆弄了起来，好像不知道该挂在哪儿似的。
有什么不对吗？你问她。
她看看你，看看徽章，也说不出个所以然。
没过一会儿，她就又恢复了往日的那副活泼模样，所以你也没过多在意这件事。当她重新跟你提起那枚徽章的时候，你甚至愣了一下。
她知道哪里不对了，她说。
如果当初，花椰菜那些驮兽没被丢在战场上，也没有遇到她，那他们大概会在战争结束后被集中拍卖。那些还算健康的被人买去干农活，剩下的就地宰杀，便宜卖肉。那之后，军队里管理驮兽的驯兽官，会得到一枚由祭司亲手颁发的，象征英雄首肯的战功徽章。
徽章在她眼里一直都是那样的东西。可是从那时候到现在，她和驮兽们唯一做过的事，就是拼了命地活下去。而活下去，大概不是什么该被授勋奖励的事。
那徽章怎么办呢？你问。
已经交给里底娅小姐了，她说。政府上次做公民身份普查的时候，她手上既没有出生证明也没有身份证件，就把那枚徽章给出去了。
“有人给我发了这玩意，用来表彰我特别努力地活着。那你们就拿它当那份证明吧，证明我出生了，我还活着，我没死掉——不管你们需要的是什么。”
